## Research reference

Feed is a major cost in fish farming. [NOAA](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/insight/feeds-aquaculture) describes using cameras to monitor consumption and avoid overfeeding. This is the problem that motivated FeedWatch.

I trained the model using part of [AV-FFIA, by Meng Cui and colleagues](https://arxiv.org/html/2309.05058v3#S5). The dataset contains videos labeled by feeding intensity with guidance from a technician. The U-FFIA study uses these data to investigate feeding activity recognition.
A análise utiliza 16 imagens a cada dois: The analysis uses 16 images every two seconds. A frozen MobileNetV3 Small extracts features, and a GRU trained in this project estimates the feeding activity category. The two Fishial detectors and the tracker detect and follow fish separately. Technical files retain the original category names: none, weak, medium and strong. The interface displays them as not observed, low, moderate and high.
Resultados históricos indisponíveis. Con: Historical results are unavailable. See the reports below.
O teste histórico não mede o acerto do v: The historical test does not measure accuracy on your uploaded video. Recall for the moderate category was **18.31%**. The GRU did not consistently outperform the Random Forest or show a clear benefit from temporal order. One held-out day does not represent other farms or cameras. Scores are not calibrated confidence.
Protótipo experimental. A classificação: Experimental prototype. The classification estimates feeding intensity; it does not determine hunger, satiety or feed dosage.
